posts.hook: Kolagen yang anda minum tak 'terus sampai' ke kulit. Badan tak berfungsi macam tu.

bm.instagram:
Ramai jenama nutricosmetic (kolagen minum, probiotik, beauty drink) pasarkan macam ia serum dalam botol: telan sahaja, kesan terus kena kulit.

Bukan macam tu ia berfungsi. Kajian ulasan gut-skin axis (Nutrients, 16 Sept 2026) terangkan laluan sebenar: mikrobiom usus hasilkan metabolit, contoh short-chain fatty acids, dan metabolit inilah yang beri kesan pada kulit melalui isyarat sistemik atau imun. Bahan asal yang anda telan tak 'sampai' ke kulit dalam bentuk asal. Ia lebih rumit daripada 'minum kolagen, kulit dapat kolagen'.

Untuk SME yang jual produk sebegini, ini bukan soal sains sahaja, ini soal dakwaan. Kalau nak dakwa kesan pada kulit, dakwaan tu kena sandar pada laluan metabolik yang memang dikaji untuk bahan spesifik anda, contoh strain probiotik tertentu atau serat yang menghasilkan metabolit tertentu. Bukan andaian umum yang belum tentu terpakai pada formulasi anda.

Produk minum yang dakwa kesan kulit tanpa mekanisme yang disokong kajian, berisiko dianggap dakwaan tanpa bukti bila kena semakan iklan NPRA atau KKM.
bm.facebook:
Nutricosmetic (kolagen minum, probiotik, beauty drink) selalu dipasarkan macam serum dalam botol: telan, kesan terus kena kulit.

Mekanisme sebenar tak begitu. Kajian ulasan gut-skin axis (Nutrients, 16 Sept 2026) tunjukkan mikrobiom usus hasilkan metabolit (contoh short-chain fatty acids) yang beri kesan pada kulit melalui isyarat sistemik, bukan bahan asal yang 'sampai' ke kulit.

Kalau produk anda nak dakwa kesan kulit, dakwaan tu kena sandar pada laluan metabolik yang dikaji untuk bahan spesifik anda punya, bukan andaian umum. Dakwaan yang tak sandar begitu berisiko kena tolak semasa semakan iklan NPRA/KKM.
bm.threads: Kolagen minum tak 'terus jadi' kolagen kulit. Kajian gut-skin axis (Nutrients, 16 Sept 2026) tunjukkan mikrobiom usus hasilkan metabolit yang beri kesan melalui isyarat sistemik, bukan bahan asal yang sampai ke kulit. Dakwaan kesan kulit kena sandar pada mekanisme spesifik bahan anda, bukan andaian umum. Kalau tak, itu dakwaan tanpa bukti bila kena semakan iklan.

en.instagram:
A lot of nutricosmetic brands (collagen drinks, probiotics, beauty drinks) get marketed like a serum in a bottle: drink it, the effect lands straight on your skin.

That is not how it works. A review study on the gut-skin axis (Nutrients, 16 Sept 2026) lays out the actual mechanism: gut microbiome produces metabolites, short-chain fatty acids for example, and those metabolites affect skin through systemic or immune signalling. The original ingredient does not 'arrive' at the skin in its original form. It is more complicated than 'drink collagen, get collagen skin'.

For SMEs selling these products, this is not just a science point, it is a claims point. If you want to claim a skin effect, that claim needs to sit on a metabolic pathway that has actually been studied for your specific ingredient, a particular probiotic strain or a fibre that produces a specific metabolite. Not a general assumption that may not even apply to your formulation.

A drink product claiming skin effects without an ingredient whose mechanism is backed by this kind of research risks being treated as an unsubstantiated claim under NPRA or KKM advertisement review.

posts.hook: The EU has notified the WTO of another cosmetics ingredient clean-up, and the comment window has already closed.

bm.linkedin:
EU baru memaklumkan WTO satu lagi pembersihan senarai bahan kosmetik, dan tempoh maklum balas sudah pun tutup.

G/TBT/N/EU/1219 diterima pada 8 Julai 2026. Ia draf Peraturan Suruhanjaya yang meminda Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 berkaitan bahan karsinogenik, mutagenik atau toksik dalam kosmetik.

Lima bahan masuk senarai larangan: Benzophenone-1, Benzophenone-2, Basic Brown 16, Basic Blue 99 dan prostaglandin analogues. Butylated hydroxyanisole, butylparaben, cannabidiol dan nano hydroxyapatite dihadkan, bukan diharamkan. Baki derogation untuk pengawet bermerkuri dibuang.

Maklum balas ditutup pada 6 September 2026. Notifikasi mencadangkan berkuat kuasa pada 1 Februari 2027 dan tidak menyatakan tarikh penerimaan pakai.

Kalau anda eksport ke EU atau formulasi ikut had EU, latihan yang berguna cuma satu. Semak senarai INCI semasa terhadap sembilan nama itu sebelum teks muktamad, kerana draf yang sudah melepasi konsultasi jarang menjadi lebih longgar.

Sources: WTO TBT notification G/TBT/N/EU/1219, European Commission, distributed 8 July 2026 (draft amending Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009)

#RegulatoryAffairs #WTOTBT #CosmeticRegulation #EUCosmetics

en.linkedin:
The EU has notified the WTO of another cosmetics ingredient clean-up, and the comment window has already closed.

G/TBT/N/EU/1219 arrived on 8 July 2026. It is a draft Commission Regulation amending Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 on carcinogenic, mutagenic or toxic substances in cosmetics.

Five substances move into the prohibited list: Benzophenone-1, Benzophenone-2, Basic Brown 16, Basic Blue 99 and prostaglandin analogues. Butylated hydroxyanisole, butylparaben, cannabidiol and nano hydroxyapatite are restricted rather than banned. The remaining derogations for mercury-containing preservatives are removed.

Comments closed on 6 September 2026. The notification proposes entry into force on 1 February 2027 and does not state an adoption date.

If you export to the EU or formulate to EU limits, the useful exercise is a simple one. Check your current INCI lists against those nine names before the text is final, because a draft that has cleared consultation rarely gets softer.

Sources: WTO TBT notification G/TBT/N/EU/1219, European Commission, distributed 8 July 2026 (draft amending Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009)

#RegulatoryAffairs #WTOTBT #CosmeticRegulation #EUCosmetics

posts.hook: Semua barang kat rak tu bersijil halal, jadi kedai runcit tu automatik "halal" juga? Tak begitu.

bm.instagram:
Ramai anggap kalau kebanyakan produk kat kedai runcit atau minimarket bersijil halal, kedai itu sendiri jadi "halal". Ini silap konsep yang JAKIM sendiri dah betulkan dalam laman Isu-Isu Tular Halal rasmi mereka.

Premis jenis peruncitan, iaitu kedai runcit dan minimarket, pada asasnya bukan pemegang Sijil Pengesahan Halal Malaysia (SPHM). JAKIM tidak pernah mengeluarkan pensijilan halal untuk konsep peruncitan itu sendiri.

SPHM disijilkan ikut skim: produk, premis makanan (foodservice), rumah sembelihan, dan beberapa skim lain. Peruncitan bukan salah satu daripadanya.

Jadi bila anda masuk kedai runcit, soalan yang patut ditanya bukan "kedai ni halal ke tak". Soalan sebenar: produk yang anda beli tu ada sijil sendiri ke tak, dan macam mana kedai itu asingkan barang halal dan tidak halal kat rak yang sama.

Untuk pengusaha yang bekalkan produk ke kedai runcit atau minimarket, perkara ini penting juga. Sijil yang sah tu melekat pada produk anda punya nama, bukan pada reputasi kedai tempat ia dijual.
bm.facebook:
Ramai anggap kalau kebanyakan produk kat kedai runcit bersijil halal, kedai itu sendiri jadi "halal". JAKIM dah betulkan ini dalam laman Isu-Isu Tular Halal rasmi: premis peruncitan bukan pemegang SPHM, dan JAKIM tak pernah sijilkan konsep peruncitan.

SPHM disijilkan ikut skim: produk, premis makanan, rumah sembelihan. Peruncitan bukan salah satunya.

Soalan yang patut ditanya bukan "kedai ni halal ke tak", tapi produk yang anda beli tu ada sijil sendiri ke tak, dan macam mana kedai itu asingkan barang di rak yang sama.
bm.threads: Kedai runcit bukan pemegang SPHM walaupun rak dia penuh produk bersijil halal. JAKIM dah confirm ni dalam laman Isu-Isu Tular Halal: pensijilan halal ikut skim, produk atau premis makanan, bukan skim peruncitan. Soalan yang betul: produk tu ada sijil sendiri ke tak.

en.instagram:
A lot of people assume that if most products on a grocery store's shelves carry a halal certificate, the store itself is "halal". JAKIM corrected this misconception directly on their official Isu-Isu Tular Halal page.

Retail-type premises, meaning grocery stores and minimarkets, are fundamentally not holders of the Sijil Pengesahan Halal Malaysia (SPHM). JAKIM has never issued halal certification for the retail concept itself.

SPHM is certified by scheme: product, food premise (foodservice), slaughterhouse, and a few others. Retail is not one of them.

So when you walk into a grocery store, the question isn't "is this shop halal". The real question is whether the specific product you're buying has its own certificate, and how the shop separates halal and non-halal items on the same shelf.

For businesses supplying grocery stores or minimarkets, this matters too. A valid certificate belongs to your product's name, not to the reputation of the shop it's sold in.
en.facebook:
Many assume that if most products in a grocery store carry halal certificates, the store itself is "halal". JAKIM has clarified this on their official Isu-Isu Tular Halal page: retail premises are not SPHM holders, and JAKIM has never certified the retail concept itself.

SPHM is certified by scheme: product, food premise, slaughterhouse. Retail isn't one of them.

The question to ask isn't "is this shop halal", it's whether the product you're buying has its own certificate, and how the shelf is managed.
en.threads: A grocery store isn't an SPHM holder even if every product on its shelf is halal certified. JAKIM confirmed this on their Isu-Isu Tular Halal page: certification runs by scheme, product or food premise, not a retail scheme. The right question is whether the product itself is certified.

posts.hook: Logo badan pensijilan yang diiktiraf pada produk pelik? Itu bukan salah badan tu, itu salah syarikat yang letak logo.

bm.instagram:
Ramai nampak logo badan pensijilan halal luar negara pada sesuatu produk yang label dia sendiri sebut ada unsur tidak halal, terus buat kesimpulan badan pensijilan tu longgar atau tak boleh dipercayai. Ni salah faham yang kerap berlaku.

JAKIM mengiktiraf BADAN pensijilan, bukan produk. Pengiktirafan tu bermaksud badan tersebut punya sistem dan kredibiliti yang JAKIM terima. Tapi sijil sebenar untuk sesuatu produk dikeluarkan secara berasingan, per produk, per kilang. Satu badan boleh sijilkan ratusan produk, dan tak semua produk syarikat yang sama automatik masuk senarai tu.

Jadi bila anda nampak logo halal pada produk yang buat anda tertanya-tanya, soalan yang patut ditanya bukan 'kenapa badan ni sijilkan benda macam ni'. Soalan yang betul: 'produk ni memang ada dalam senarai sijil badan tu ke tidak'. Kalau logo ada tapi produk tak wujud dalam senarai, itu penyalahgunaan logo oleh syarikat pengeluar, bukan kegagalan badan pensijilan.

Untuk pengimport: sebelum bawa masuk atau edarkan produk berlogo halal, semak status sijil produk tu sendiri. Jangan bergantung pada logo je.
bm.facebook:
Logo badan pensijilan halal luar negara yang diiktiraf JAKIM pada sesuatu produk tak bermakna produk tu disijilkan. Pengiktirafan JAKIM diberi pada badan, bukan pada setiap produk yang bawa logonya. Sijil sebenar dikeluarkan per produk, per kilang, dan boleh disemak.

Jadi bila nampak logo pada produk yang pelik, soalan betul bukan 'kenapa badan tu sijilkan ni' tapi 'produk ni ada dalam senarai sijil badan tu ke tidak'. Kalau tiada, itu salah guna logo oleh syarikat, bukan kelemahan badan pensijilan.

Untuk pengimport: semak status sijil produk, bukan status pengiktirafan badan sahaja.
bm.threads: Logo badan halal luar negara yang diiktiraf JAKIM pada produk tak bermakna produk tu disijilkan. Pengiktirafan tu untuk badan, bukan setiap produk yang bawa logonya. Sijil sebenar per produk, per kilang, dan boleh disemak. Kalau produk tak ada dalam senarai sijil, itu salah guna logo, bukan kegagalan badan. Semak produk, bukan cuma logo.

en.instagram:
People see a recognised foreign halal certification body's logo on a product whose own label mentions a non-halal ingredient, and jump to 'this certification body is unreliable'. That is the wrong read.

JAKIM's recognition is given to the certification BODY, not to every product carrying its logo. Recognition means JAKIM accepts that body's system and credibility. But the actual certificate for a specific product is issued separately, per product, per factory. One recognised body can certify hundreds of products, and not every product from the same manufacturer is automatically on that list.

So when you see a halal logo on a product that looks off, the question is not 'why did this body certify something like this'. The right question is 'is this exact product actually on that body's certified list'. If the logo is there but the product is not on the list, that is logo misuse by the manufacturer, not a failure of the certification body.

For importers: before you bring in or distribute a product with a halal logo, check the certificate status of that specific product. Don't take the logo at face value.
en.facebook:
A recognised foreign halal certification body's logo on a product does not mean that product is certified. JAKIM's recognition applies to the body, not to every product bearing its logo. The actual certificate is issued per product, per factory, and it is checkable.

So when a logo shows up on a product that looks wrong, the right question isn't 'why did this body certify this'. It's 'is this product actually on that body's certified list'. If it isn't, that's logo misuse by the manufacturer, not a certification body failure.

For importers: check the product's own certificate status, not just the body's recognition status.
en.threads: A recognised foreign halal body's logo on a product doesn't mean that product is certified. JAKIM recognises the BODY, not every product carrying its logo. Certificates are issued per product, per factory, and checkable. If a product isn't on that body's list, it's logo misuse, not a certification body failure.

posts.hook: Ada sijil halal tak bermakna semua yang anda jual atau semua premis anda halal.

bm.instagram:
Isu ini tular sejak beberapa hari lepas pasal status halal sebuah premis minuman herba. JAKIM sudah jelaskan: syarikat itu memang ada Sijil Pengesahan Halal Malaysia yang sah, tapi untuk skim produk makanan dan minuman, khusus untuk minuman herba bertin. Bukan untuk skim premis makanan.

Ramai usahawan silap faham benda ni. SPHM bukan satu sijil sepadu yang automatik cover segala-galanya di bawah nama syarikat anda. JAKIM keluarkan sijil ikut SKIM: rumah sembelihan, makanan, premis makanan, kosmetik, logistik, dan lain-lain. Setiap skim ada permohonan sendiri, penilaian sendiri, dan skop sendiri.

Syarikat anda boleh ada SPHM sah untuk satu produk botol atau tin, tapi kalau seseorang semak sijil itu untuk premis atau produk lain yang tak pernah dipohon, ia akan nampak macam tak halal. Bukan sijil palsu, cuma skop tak sama.

Bila anda semak status halal syarikat lain (atau sendiri), jangan tanya 'ada sijil ke tak'. Tanya 'sijil ini cover skim apa, produk atau premis yang mana'. Semak terus kat portal MYeHALAL, bukan ikut apa yang dilekat kat botol atau signboard.

Untuk pengusaha yang baru nak mohon: kalau anda ada lebih satu lini produk atau lebih satu premis, anda kena fikir dari awal sama ada perlu mohon lebih daripada satu skim. Ini bukan kos tambahan yang boleh dielak, ini keperluan asas skop sijil.
bm.facebook:
Isu tular pasal status halal sebuah premis minuman herba. JAKIM sudah jelaskan: syarikat itu ada SPHM sah, tapi untuk skim minuman herba bertin sahaja, bukan skim premis makanan.

Ramai silap faham SPHM ni satu sijil sepadu yang cover semua bawah nama syarikat. Sebenarnya JAKIM keluarkan ikut SKIM (rumah sembelihan, makanan, premis, kosmetik, logistik) dan ikut produk atau premis yang dipohon khusus.

Ada SPHM untuk satu produk tak bermakna semua premis atau produk lain syarikat sama automatik halal. Semak skop, bukan sekadar 'ada sijil atau tak'.
bm.threads: JAKIM dah klarifikasi: sijil halal syarikat minuman herba itu sah, tapi untuk skim produk sahaja, bukan premis. SPHM bukan sijil sepadu. Ia ikut skim: makanan, premis, kosmetik, logistik, masing-masing dipohon berasingan. Ada sijil untuk satu produk tak sama dengan ada sijil untuk semua.

en.instagram:
A halal status issue about an herbal drink premise has been going around. JAKIM has clarified: the company does hold a valid Malaysia Halal Certification, but under the food and beverage product scheme, specifically for canned herbal drinks. Not under the food premise scheme.

This mix-up is common. SPHM is not one blanket certificate covering everything under a company's name. JAKIM issues certification by SCHEME: slaughterhouse, food, food premise, cosmetics, logistics, and others. Each scheme is a separate application with its own scope.

A company can hold a valid SPHM for one bottled or canned product and still fail scrutiny if someone checks that certificate against a different premise or product that was never applied for. It is not a fake certificate. The scope simply does not extend that far.

When checking halal status, whether your own or someone else's, do not ask 'is there a certificate'. Ask 'which scheme, which product or premise does this certificate actually cover'. Check directly on MYeHALAL, not by what is printed on a bottle or signboard.

If you run more than one product line or more than one premise, you need to plan from the start whether you need to apply under more than one scheme. That is not an avoidable extra cost, it is basic scope requirement.
en.facebook:
A halal status issue about an herbal drink premise has circulated recently. JAKIM clarified: the company holds a valid SPHM, but under the beverage product scheme for canned herbal drinks, not the food premise scheme.

SPHM is not a blanket certificate covering everything under a company name. JAKIM issues it by scheme, food, premise, cosmetics, logistics, each applied for separately.

Holding a certificate for one product does not mean every premise or product under the same company is covered. Check the scope, not just whether a certificate exists.
en.threads: JAKIM clarified: the herbal drink company's halal cert is valid, but only for the product scheme, not the premise scheme. SPHM is not a blanket certificate. It runs by scheme, food, premise, cosmetics, logistics, each applied separately. One certified product does not mean everything is certified.
